newsitem.title: UK: Japan funds perk up on Nikkei outlook - survey.
newsitem.headline: Japan funds perk up on Nikkei outlook - survey.

text.p: Japanese fund managers are becoming more optimistic on the outlook for the Japanese economy, and as a result are turning bullish on prospects for the stock market, a survey by Merrill Lynch showed.
On a year's view, bulls outnumber bears by 60 percent on prospects for the Nikkei, it said.

The survey showed that the trend among Japanese fund managers was away from reducing exposure to U.S. equities, while they were buyers of European equities, sellers of UK equities, picking up Asian equities, and were no longer reducing cash.
There were fewer sellers of Japanese bonds while they remained keen buyers of bonds outside Japan.
The survey showed they were generally bearish on the outlook for equities over three months, but bullish on a 12 month view.
The survey was carried out by Gallup on behalf of Merrill Lynch between March 3 and 4, covering 42 institutions responsible for funds totalling $560 billion.
